brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor execution: growth stages (seed→sprout→bloom) map directly to streak length, making state legible at a glance
Warm, cohesive sky-to-grass gradient with sun and cloud creates genuine emotional warmth and reinforces the garden world
Emoji-based plant illustrations carry charm and avoid the sterility typical of habit trackers
dominant_weaknesses: Massive empty mid-canvas: plants float in a thin band at the top while two-thirds of the screen is unused gradient
Streak number badges feel like generic notification dots, breaking the illustrative metaphor with flat UI chrome
Typography is serif-display title over sans labels with no clear hierarchy system; the 'Coding / Needs water' wilt state is barely differentiated visually
fix_priorities: Rebalance vertical composition — either enlarge plant beds, add ground/horizon line, or stack rows so the garden fills the frame
Replace badge counters with diegetic indicators (rings on stem, petals, soil moisture) so streaks live inside the metaphor
Strengthen the wilt/neglect state with drooping posture, browned leaves, or dry soil — currently 'Needs water' reads as text, not visual
Unify type system: pick one family or pair intentionally, and give streak labels a quieter weight than habit names
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral charm leads, behavioral feedback is moderate (clear states but weak neglect cue), reflective payoff is decent through the growth narrative.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the garden metaphor is executed literally and legibly, but composition and state-differentiation hold it back from feeling alive.
